registry.headline: Content source check: possible problems found ({count}) — a bonus may not work, or content may not appear or may show wrongly; see {log}. This is only a notice; the export was not blocked.
registry.log.title: Content source check (notices only)
registry.log.rules: Modifier names were checked against the CWTools rules {repository} {commit} ({license}).
registry.log.no_rules: The CWTools rules ({file}) were not found, so modifier names were not checked. Get them from {repository} ({license}) and put them in {folder} next to the program, or choose their folder in Settings.
registry.log.notes:
A large base mod can add content when the game loads. "Source not registered" means this export alone cannot show where something comes from: register or import the base mod, or change the file named on the line.
This check never deletes, rewrites or blocks anything.
registry.modifier_unknown: Modifier "{name}" is not in the game's data or in this mod's modifier_definitions, so the game may ignore this bonus. Correct the name here, or define it in common/modifier_definitions.
registry.idea_category_unregistered: Idea category "{name}" is not defined by the base game or by common/idea_tags in this export, so national spirits in it may not appear. Register or import the base mod's idea_tags, or change or add this category.
registry.idea_slot_unregistered: National spirit or advisor slot "{name}" is not defined by the base game or by common/idea_tags in this export, so this content may have nowhere to appear. Register or import the base mod's idea_tags, or change this slot.
registry.script_id_non_ascii: Script ID "{id}" contains Chinese or other non-ASCII characters, so the game may fail to register or find it. Rename it here using English letters, digits and underscores, and update its references and localisation keys to match.
registry.instance_allowed_first: A character instance must start with allowed = { ... }, or the game may pick the wrong version or ignore this one. Add allowed to this instance and move it to the top.
registry.character_vanilla_id: Character ID "{id}" is already used by the base game. Adding a file loads both definitions, and the character may be recruitable twice. Rename it, or change the original file instead of adding a second definition.
registry.flags_unregistered: These flags of {tag} have no registered source in this export: {files}. The diplomacy screen, unit markers or flags in text may show empty or wrong. Register or import the base mod's flags, or add all three sizes under gfx/flags.
refs.headline.broken_and_review: Script reference check: references to something this export does not contain ({broken}) — the units or focus paths involved will not work (see {log}); also needing a designer's look: {review}. The export was not blocked.
refs.headline.broken: Script reference check: references to something this export does not contain ({broken}) — the units or focus paths involved will not work (see {log}). The export was not blocked.
refs.headline.review: Script reference check: relationships that need a designer's look ({review}). The export was not blocked.
refs.log.title: Script reference check (notices only; they never stop the export)
refs.log.notes:
This checks the files the player downloads; content from the workbenches and raw files is held to the same standard.
Nothing is rewritten for you. When a large base mod is not registered, the check can only say that a source is not registered.
refs.focus_case.summary: Focus "{focus}" names its {relation} as "{target}", but that focus is defined as "{exact}" (letter case must match exactly).
refs.focus_case.impact: This focus path may not unlock or exclude as planned.
refs.focus_case.edit: In the focus tree, change this reference to "{exact}".
refs.focus_missing.summary: The {relation} "{target}" of focus "{focus}" is not in this export.
refs.focus_unregistered.summary: The {relation} "{target}" of focus "{focus}" has no registered source. It may come from a large base mod, so this does not prove it is missing.
refs.focus_missing.impact: Players may be unable to continue this focus path, and a reference to a focus that does not exist can also stop the game from loading.
refs.focus_missing.edit: The focus tree's prerequisite and mutually exclusive settings. If the focus comes from a base mod, register that source first and check again.
refs.completed_case.summary: The "completed focus" condition says "{target}", but the focus ID is "{exact}" (letter case must match exactly).
refs.completed_case.impact: The condition may never be met, so the events, decisions or focus rewards that follow will not appear.
refs.completed_case.edit: In this script's has_completed_focus, change the value to "{exact}".
refs.template_missing.summary: {tag} is to spawn "{template}" units, but its starting division templates have none of that name.
refs.template_unregistered.summary: {tag} uses division template "{template}", but the template has no registered source. It may come from a large base mod, so this does not prove it is missing.
refs.template.impact: These starting units, or the units an event creates, may not appear.
refs.template.edit: Add a division template of that name for {tag} under Division templates, or change division_template to a template {tag} already has.
newline.headline: Literal \n in the exported files ({count}): the game may read each such passage as one long line, so what follows will not take effect. Fix them at the files and positions listed in {log}.
newline.log.header:
Literal \n check
The game may read each passage below as one long line, so what follows will not take effect. Replace the \n with a real line break at each position.
Format: file:line:column | text
newline.finding.impact: The game may read this passage as one long line, so what follows will not take effect.
newline.finding.edit: Replace it with a real line break at the file, line and column listed in the report.
idea_picture.warning: Idea picture left out: idea "{idea}" asks for picture "{picture}", but no art was uploaded for it and "{sprite}" is not a sprite the base game defines (and this project is not a submod), so the picture line was left out of common/ideas. In game the national spirit shows a broken "?" icon in the politics panel instead of the art you chose. To fix it, upload an icon for this idea, point picture at a base-game sprite that exists, or define the sprite in this mod with an interface/*.gfx raw file.
idea_picture.message: Idea "{idea}" asks for picture "{picture}", but the export has no art for it and "{sprite}" is not a sprite the base game defines, so the picture line was left out of the generated common/ideas file.
idea_picture.impact: The national spirit shows a broken "?" icon in the country's politics panel instead of the chosen art. Its modifiers still apply; only the picture is missing.
idea_picture.edit: Fix it on this idea in the Ideas workbench in one of three ways: upload an icon for the idea; point picture at a base-game sprite that exists; or add an interface/*.gfx definition for "{sprite}" to this mod as a raw file.
idea_picture.edit_with_names: Fix it on this idea in the Ideas workbench in one of three ways: upload an icon for the idea; point picture at a base-game sprite that exists (closest existing names: {names}); or add an interface/*.gfx definition for "{sprite}" to this mod as a raw file.
dlc.headline: Blocks that need a DLC (has_dlc): {blocks}; DLCs involved: {count} ({names}). They run only for players who own that DLC — check {log} ({dir}: {dir_count}).
dlc.log.header:
Blocks that depend on a DLC
Every has_dlc = "<name>" in the exported script, with the block it guards. A guarded block runs only for players who own that DLC (a NOT guard runs only for players who do not). If you own every DLC, these blocks always ran for you and never for a player without the DLC — the mod works on your machine and crashes for them.
Nothing here is an error and nothing was changed. Check each block and make sure the mod still works when it does not run.
"unknown" means the name is not a known DLC name; with a typo the block never runs for anyone.

Columns: <path>:<line>  [NOT] has_dlc "<name>"  <context>  -> <guarded effect keys>
loc_fallback.headline: Untranslated text: {fallback} of {total} keys ({percent}) still show the English text in {languages}. Translate them to clear the list in {log}.
loc_fallback.log.header:
Untranslated text
A key is listed when its text is not empty, is exactly the same as the English text of the same key, and has at least three Latin letters in a row. The English text was written on purpose: in game it is better than a bare key. Translate the text to clear a line. This never blocks the export.
image.skipped: Picture left out: {item} — its image could not be read. The rest of the mod was exported normally.
super_event.dormant: Super event left out: "{id}" — nothing in this project fires it (no event, decision, focus or file refers to it, and it does not fire on its own), so its script, picture and localisation were not exported. Give it a trigger, or ignore this if it is meant to be unused.
focus.shared_layout_raw: {file}: a raw file of yours controls the exported shared focus layout, so the program's shared focus placement may not apply. Check this file's conditional offsets.
flags.missing: Countries whose flag could not be exported ({count}): {tags}. A flag is on record for them, but this export has no usable image, so in game they show the base game's flag or a blank one.
cover.only_thumbnail: The mod's cover picture was left out of the descriptor: only {file} is supported.
cover.unreadable: The mod's cover picture was left out of the descriptor: {file} could not be read.
raw_override.log.header:
Raw override files
Each file below was written exactly as you wrote it, at its path, without any of the program's checks. The program did not read or check its contents — making it correct is up to you.
collision.log.header:
Files that replace base-game files
Each path below is the same as a base-game file's path and replaces that file in game — HOI4 does not merge files with the same path. These are icon or bookmark replacements: if you meant to replace the base game's version, all is well; if the names match by accident, rename the item's ID so its file no longer matches. This never blocks the export.
duplicate.image: The same image was exported for two different items: "{first}" ({first_source}) and "{second}" ({second_source}) are identical, so one of them has probably lost its own upload. Upload that one again and export again.
preserved_loc.bad_source: Imported localisation lines left out ({count}): their source file is not a localisation/**/*.yml path inside the mod.
preserved_loc.bad_key: Imported localisation keys left out ({count}): a localisation key may only contain A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -, and anything else breaks every line after it in the same file. Left out: {keys}
gui.reason.no_access: the project's uploaded files could not be opened
gui.reason.snapshot_unread: the imported interface snapshot could not be read
gui.reason.snapshot_broken: the imported interface snapshot is damaged
gui.overlays_skipped: Interface edits left out: {reason}. The rest of the mod was exported normally.
gui.overlay_no_scaffold: Interface edits to "{file}" left out: the interface file they were made against is not stored with the project. Save the screen again in the game view to fix this. The rest of the mod was exported normally.
gui.overlay_unreadable: Interface edits to "{file}" left out: its interface file could not be read back ({reason}). The rest of the mod was exported normally.
gui.swap_engine_picture: Picture swap in "{file}" left out: swap_sprite on {target} points the main menu background or the loading screen at another picture, but the game swaps that picture itself and stops drawing (the GPU stops responding on the main menu). Replace the background picture in the game view instead. The other interface edits were exported normally.
gui.swap_no_upload: Picture swap in "{file}" left out: swap_sprite on {target} wants "{picture}", but no uploaded file was found for it, so the original picture stays. The other interface edits were exported normally.
gui.orphan_edits: Interface edits in "{file}" left out ({count}): {targets} — these elements are no longer in the imported interface file. The other interface edits were exported normally.
ui_baseline.skipped: The imported mod's own interface files were left out: {reason}. The rest of the mod was exported normally.
ui_baseline.reason.metadata: the list of imported interface files could not be read
ui_baseline.reason.case_collision: the imported interface snapshot has paths that differ only in letter case
character.vanilla_id: Character "{tag}" reuses a base-game character ID, so the game loads both definitions (game error: "Multiple character have the tag"). A mod only replaces base-game content by using the same file name, and this export never does — rename the character, or change the base-game one instead of defining it again.
character.vanilla_id_recruited_twice: Character "{tag}" reuses a base-game character ID, so the game loads both definitions (game error: "Multiple character have the tag") and recruits the character twice (game error: "already assigned"). A mod only replaces base-game content by using the same file name, and this export never does — rename the character, or change the base-game one instead of defining it again.
ideology.skipped: {reason}, so the inherited ideology subtypes {subtypes} are not applied — add them to the project's own ideology file.
ideology.relocked: the mod's ideology files were imported again after the inherited ideology subtypes {subtypes} were confirmed; they were applied to the current files.
ideology.reason.replace_path: replace_path=common/ideologies replaces the base game's ideologies
ideology.reason.own_file: the project's own {file} takes over common/ideologies
ideology.reason.reimported: the mod's ideology files were imported again after these subtypes were confirmed, and they no longer fit there ({codes})
syntax.warning.attention: Exported file needs attention: {path}:{line} [{code}] {detail} | nearby: {snippet} | player impact: {impact} | fix in: {edit}
syntax.warning.review: Exported file worth a look: {path}:{line} [{code}] {detail} | nearby: {snippet} | player impact: {impact} | fix in: {edit}
syntax.detail.unknown_token: the parser ignored the unrecognised token "{token}"
syntax.detail.unterminated_quote: quoted text runs to the end of the file without a closing quote
syntax.detail.literal_newline: a literal \n appears in the script outside a quoted value
syntax.detail.anonymous_block: an unnamed { ... } wrapper at the top of the file looks like generated pseudo-structure
syntax.detail.bare_token: the bare token "{token}" at the top of the file has no setting name
syntax.detail.missing_bom: the localisation file is not saved as UTF-8 with BOM
syntax.detail.second_header: a second language header starts inside the same file
syntax.detail.unknown_language: language header "{language}" is not one of the languages HOI4 supports
syntax.detail.before_header: text comes before the required l_* language header
syntax.detail.no_header: no l_* language header was found
syntax.detail.invalid_key: key "{key}" contains a character HOI4 localisation keys do not allow
syntax.detail.missing_open_quote: the localisation text must start with a quote
syntax.detail.unterminated_value: the localisation text has no closing quote on this line
syntax.detail.trailing_junk: unexpected text follows the closing quote
syntax.impact.script: HOI4 may stop reading this file here, so later game content can disappear or fail to load.
syntax.impact.localisation: Text from this point on can disappear or show raw keys to the player.
syntax.impact.missing_bom: This text file can load unreliably and show localisation keys instead of text.
crossref.log.header:
References between workbenches (notices only)
No assignment in your content was deleted or rewritten. Check the IDs that could not be found and fix them yourself if needed.
This was built by scanning the finished export, so each line names the file it was found in and the line:column inside that file.
Reference types checked: {types}.
That is every type the program models. Each ID was looked up in this project's own content and in the base game; IDs a base mod adds when the game loads are in neither, so in a submod those lines say base_mod_not_indexed instead of missing.
token.log.header:
Unknown tokens
Each line is a token the program does not know from the base game, with how often it appears. The category of add_tech_bonus / has_tech_bonus must be a real technology category (construction_tech / industry / electronics — not construction).
Custom or base-mod tokens are valid in HOI4 — check before assuming a mistake. This file never blocks the export.
Categories this export declares itself in common/technology_tags/ count as valid and are not listed.
scripted.log.header: `<name> = yes|no` calls whose name is not a base-game effect or trigger, not a field the program knows, and not defined by this export under common/scripted_effects/ or common/scripted_triggers/. This is not a broken reference: each call is kept as written and works only if a base mod or raw file defines it. Nothing here blocks the export.
scripted.headline: Custom scripted effects or triggers the program does not know ({count}): {names}. They are kept as written and work only if a base mod or raw file defines them — see {log}.
placeholder.headline: Workbench placeholder IDs ({count}): {ids}. The game has no name for these and shows the raw ID instead; rename them in the workbench ({tables}).
focus.tree_assigned: the focus tree has no country of its own, so it was given to the project's main country {tag} so that it can be picked in game
focus.tree_no_country: the focus tree has no country, and the project has no main country either — no country can pick this tree, so its focus screen stays empty in game
focus.tree_empty_list: the focus tree is limited to a list of countries, but the list is empty — no country can pick this tree
focus.tree_unknown_scope: the focus tree has an unknown scope {scope} — no country block was written, so no country can pick this tree
focus.shared_offset_not_integer: Shared focus {focus} in {tree}: its placement offset was not exported because its coordinates are not whole numbers.
focus.shared_offset_unresolved: Shared focus {focus} in {tree}: its placement offset was not exported because its tree or shared definition is missing, ambiguous or not supported.
politics.headline: Politics export: warnings for {subjects} ({count}) — part of their history or politics was dropped or skipped (ruling party, duplicate history rows, dated blocks or bookmark pictures); details in {log}.
politics.headline_unnamed: Politics export: warnings ({count}) — part of the history or politics was dropped or skipped (ruling party, duplicate history rows, dated blocks or bookmark pictures); details in {log}.
politics.headline_notes: Politics export: notes about common/ideologies and replace_path ({count}); details in {log}.
politics.log.header:
Politics and ideology export warnings
Things noticed while writing the country history files and common/ideologies that did not stop the export. Check each line before you release the mod: a dropped ruling party, two rows for the same country, or how your own ideologies were written.
politics.note.ideologies_full: common/ideologies/00_ideologies.txt was written with all of the base game's ideologies (each of the four groups defined once), your sub-ideologies added ({subs}) and your own ideology groups ({groups}), under replace_path="common/ideologies". HOI4 loads only this file for that folder, so every base-game sub-ideology (despotism and the rest) is kept and yours are defined exactly once. If you added a raw common/ideologies file as a workaround, remove it so nothing is defined twice.
politics.note.ideologies_raw: common/ideologies was not written for you: a raw file of yours already writes common/ideologies/ (your sub-ideologies: {subs}; your ideology groups: {groups}). Your raw file wins. Remove it once you rely on the ideology list, so the program writes the whole file and its replace_path for you.
politics.note.ideologies_beside: {file} was written with the project's own ideology groups ({groups}), next to the inherited ideology files (no replace_path).
politics.ideologies_missing: common/ideologies was not written: there are sub-ideologies ({subs}) and ideology groups ({groups}) of your own, but the base game's ideology file could not be read completely, so a full replacement could not be built. These sub-ideologies will not exist in game (the game crashes when one is used). Check the game folder in Settings, or add a complete common/ideologies as a raw file.
politics.bookmark_picture: {subject}: picture "{picture}" was not used, because no uploaded backdrop was found for it and it is not a base-game bookmark picture; the export uses "{fallback}" instead.
politics.duplicate_history: {subject}: a second history row turns into the same country tag (a letter-case or space variant) and would overwrite the first at {file}, so the second row was skipped. Merge the rows or fix the tag.
politics.ruling_party_dropped: {subject}: the history's ruling_party "{value}" does not belong to any ideology group that can be exported, so it was left out (writing the sub-ideology itself would be invalid in the game). Set the country's ideology to a sub-ideology of a defined group, or define your own group and its sub-ideology in the ideology list.
politics.country_ideology_dropped: {subject}: the country's ideology "{value}" does not belong to any ideology group that can be exported, so no ruling party was written for it (writing the sub-ideology itself would be invalid in the game). Put the sub-ideology under a group of your own, or pick an ideology that is defined.
politics.date_block_skipped: {subject} history file: dated block #{number} was skipped because {reason}. HOI4 writes these as `1939.9.1 = { ... }`, so the block cannot be exported without a valid date — fix it in the history workbench and export again, or what it scripts will never happen in game. The rest of this country's history was exported normally.
history_date.format: the date must look like Y.M.D or Y.M.D.H (for example 1939.1.1.12)
history_date.range: the date must use a positive year, month 1-12 and day 1-31
history_date.hour: the date's hour must be between 0 and 23
orphan.headline: State owners: states that name an unknown country tag as owner, controller or core ({count}; tags: {tags}). HOI4 reports errors when loading them — add the country to the project or fix the tag (details in {log}).
orphan.log.header:
States that name a country that does not exist
Each line is a state whose owner, controller or add_core_of names a tag that is neither a base-game country nor a country in this project. HOI4 reports an error when a state's owner is an unknown country. Fix it by adding the country to the project, correcting the typo, or importing the missing country files again.
orphan.state: State {state} ({name}): {field} = {tag} — no country in this project or the base game has this tag; HOI4 reports an error when loading.
yml.headline: Localisation: gaps between languages filled from another language ({count}): {findings}; details in {log}.
yml.log.header:
Localisation gaps between languages
Every exported language now has the same set of localisation keys.
bookmark.name_reused: {bookmark}: the bookmark has no name in {lang}, so its {fallback} name was used to keep players from seeing {key}.
bookmark.name_missing: {bookmark}: the bookmark has no name in {lang}, and no exported language has a usable one, so players will see {key}.
oob.unassigned: Order of battle: `{file}` is not loaded by any country's history, and the export could not tell which country it belongs to (its rows have no country tag, its file name does not start with one of this project's countries, nothing in it — division spawn province, fleet naval base or air wing state — lies in a state this project defines, and the project has no main country). The file is exported but the game never reads it — add `set_oob = "{stem}"` to the right country's history yourself.
oob.wired: Order of battle: nothing in your country history loaded `{file}`, so the game would have ignored everything in it. The export added `set_oob = "{stem}"` to {tag}'s history file — {tag} was chosen from {reason}. Move that line if it belongs to another country.
oob.dangling: Order of battle: {tag}'s history loads OOB file `{stem}`, but this export has no `history/units/{stem}.txt`. Unless that file comes from the base game or a mod you depend on, the line does nothing — point it at one of the OOB files this project exports ({files}) or remove it.
oob.reason.own_rows: the country tag on its own rows
oob.reason.file_prefix: the country tag its file name starts with (`{prefix}_…`), which is one of this project's own countries
oob.reason.main_country: this project's main country (its rows have no country tag, its file name does not start with one of this project's countries, and nothing in it — division spawn province, fleet naval base or air wing state — lies in a state this project defines)
oob.reason.army: the owner of the states its divisions spawn in
oob.reason.navy: the owner of the state holding the naval base its fleet is stationed at
oob.reason.air: the owner of the state its air wings are based in
job.checks_not_run: The export checks did not run, so the findings report is missing their results.
job.checks_failed: The export checks could not finish, so the findings report is incomplete.
job.checks_failed_reason: The export checks could not finish, so the findings report is incomplete ({reason}).
job.findings_not_merged: The findings report could not include the export checks' results: {reason}
